text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak says: "We are working to narrow the gap between Palestinians and Israelis for the resumption of negotiations as soon as possible." Mubarak tells CNN and the Financial Times that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu now wants peace and his stance has become more flexible.

- Mubarak and Syrian President Hafez al-Assad to co-chair the joint Egyptian-Syrian higher committee meeting in Damascus in November. The two sides signed six agreements at the final meeting of the ninth session in Cairo.
- The government allocates another 575 million pounds ($169.40 million) in the new 1997/98 budget for health, education and youth.
- Foreign Minister Amr Moussa says (Jewish) settlements will remain the main obstacle on the way towards peace. "We look forward to building good relations with Iran."
- A new round of negotiations on the Egyptian-European association agreement to be held in July.
- The Egyptian embassy in Freetown is instructed to provide protection for the Lebanese community in Sierra Leone, Moussa says.
